score.note: First pass, built from the owner's own retained assembly (games/gs1/asm/080e08c0.s) plus an m2c-assisted transplant workspace (out/family-transplants/main-080e08c0/), not from the family matcher's naive template (main:080ce85c / member_orbit/run.c), whose naive symbol-renamed seed differed from the real target by hundreds of differing halfwords. The family matcher's structural score was against member_orbit/run.c's shape, but this owner's real callee set, field layout and constants match the already-recovered 0x03001eec 'battle work' sibling cluster instead (games/gs1/recon/en/main/080e7404.c, 080d59b0.c, 080d82b0.c, 080dc1ec.c, 080e01e4.c), exactly as those five owners' own dossiers describe for their assigned (also mismatched) templates. Two real bugs found and fixed against reference evidence: (1) the CELL_W-table half-width shift in the frame>0x1F sprite-cell draw loop needs an unsigned (u32) operand to compile to lsrs -- an s32 local produced asrs, a genuine wrong-instruction, confirmed by cross-checking the already-adopted games/gs1/src/battle/effects/puff_arc/run.c, which declares the identical 'wide = CELL_W[cell]' idiom as u32 for the same reason; (2) the particle-scan draw's 'half = size >> 1' subtraction needed the same unsigned treatment (u32 cast), independently confirmed the same way. The larger single improvement (differing_halfwords 431->307, wrong_instructions 305->207, and candidate_bytes 984->968) came from restructuring the particle-scan draw call to assign 'size' inline inside the second call argument's array-index expression (Data_080ede48[(size = (member & 1) + 3) - 1]) rather than as a preceding standalone statement -- matching the established assignment-expression-as-argument idiom already proven in puff_arc/run.c's CELL_W read, and confirmed here from the reference's own instruction order (the mask/+3 sequence is interleaved with the position-read/wobble-shift sequence in the reference, not fully sequenced before it). This same change had a second, unexpected effect: it also fixed the function's very first register-allocation decision (the persistent 'work' base pointer now lands in sl for the whole function, matching the reference, instead of landing in r9) -- apparently a side effect of reduced register pressure from removing the extra 'dbl' local this change also let become an inline 'size * 2'. A fully-inlined variant that also removed the separate 'x' (position+wobble) local was tried and rejected: it lowered wrong_instructions to 209 but raised differing_halfwords 307->318, because 'size' then had to be spilled to the stack to survive the sin()-call argument evaluation; kept the version with 'x' as its own local instead, which needs no spill and scores strictly better on the primary differing_halfwords metric.
score.residual: After both fixes and the argument-order restructuring, every remaining difference is one of the three cross-family register/scheduling residuals already confirmed and explicitly flagged as not source-shape-controllable in 080dc1ec.json, 080d82b0.json, 080d59b0.json and 080e01e4.json's dossiers: (a) the ring-seed loop's inner-loop prologue loads the 0x02010000 EWRAM base constant once and reuses it via register copies for both the particle-pointer construction and the two field-8/0x14 masks, where the reference loads it twice into two separate registers (r1 and r3) -- tried giving the mask its own separate 's32 mask = 0x02010000;' local, distinct from the pointer-construction literal, which shifted which physical register (fp vs r9) holds which role but did not produce the reference's two-load shape and left differing_halfwords unchanged; (b) short-lived scratch-register choice for the outer 'frame' counter's many repeated comparisons throughout the 112-pass loop body (frame==0x38, frame<=0x17, frame==0x14, the 0x14..0x1F range fold, frame==0x20, frame>0x1F, frame==0x26) differs per comparison (r0/r1/r2/r3/r4/r6 in various orders) even though every comparison's actual VALUE, immediate and branch target are correct; (c) a handful of independent-immediate-load scheduling swaps (e.g. 'movs r3,#40' before vs after an unrelated shift-and-add sequence) that reorder two independent instructions with no value difference. None of these were resolved by variable identity consolidation (reusing one 'member' variable across all four per-pass sub-loop counters, matching 080e01e4.json's confirmed successful technique for its own sentinel-init loop, had zero measurable effect here) or declaration-order changes (moving 'work' to the first-declared local had zero effect), consistent with those dossiers' own findings that this is a genuinely open compiler-internals-level question, not a source-restructuring one.
